definitions.explanation: Originally the stone placed at the base of a building to support its structure. Now primarily used figuratively to mean the fundamental basis or groundwork upon which something important is built.

examples.japanese: ⟦{平和|へいわ}→平和：01507_heiwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{礎|いしずえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{築|きず}く→築く：02046_kizuku⟧。
examples.english: To build the foundation of peace.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{研究|けんきゅう}→研究：01396_kenkyuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{現代|げんだい}→現代：02722_gendai⟧⟦{医学|いがく}→医学：01301_igaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{礎|いしずえ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: This research became the cornerstone of modern medicine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先人|せんじん}→先人：23803_senjin⟧たち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{築|きず}いた→築く：02046_kizuku⟧{礎|いしずえ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{繁栄|はんえい}→繁栄：10131_hanei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Today's prosperity stands on the foundation that our predecessors built.

notes:
USAGE:
A literary and elevated word for foundation or basis. Almost always used figuratively in modern Japanese. The literal meaning (a foundation stone in construction) is rare outside of historical contexts.

Compare with ⟦{基盤|きばん}→基盤：00220_kiban⟧ (base, infrastructure — more concrete and practical) and ⟦{土台|どだい}→土台：07146_dodai⟧ (foundation — can be literal or figurative, less formal).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {礎|いしずえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{築|きず}く→築く：02046_kizuku⟧: to build a foundation
- {礎|いしずえ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to become a cornerstone
- {礎|いしずえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{据|す}える→据える：12796_sueru⟧: to lay a foundation
- ⟦{平和|へいわ}→平和：01507_heiwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{礎|いしずえ}: the foundation of peace
